Compute Screener

Methodology

Compute Screener, built and run by @RenshuBTC, publishes a daily GPU Price Index for each GPU family and a daily Token Price Index for each AI company. Every value is calculated automatically by the rules below and can be recomputed from the published data.

GPU Price IndexToken Price Index
MeasuresThe on-demand rental price of a GPU family at neo-cloud providers and GPU marketplacesThe posted API price of a company's models, weighted by their usage
UnitUSD / GPU-hourUSD / 1M tokens, blending 3 input tokens with 1 output token
DayCalendar day in US Central TimeUTC day
UpdatedEvery 2 to 3 hours; provisional during the day, final when it endsOnce a day, shortly after the day ends
Version4.1, from 2026-10-241.4

GPU Price Index

Indices for H100, H200, A100, B200, B300, MI300X and RTX PRO 6000. Hyperscalers such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle are not included. Every price is converted to its GPU's benchmark contract:

IndexBenchmark contract
  1. Collect. Every 2 to 3 hours, the index reads posted on-demand prices from each provider's API or pricing page: rate cards, every ask on the Vast.ai and Lium marketplaces, and Akash's average ask. Other smaller clouds are read from Shadeform's public catalog, which also shows their capacity. Each API, page or catalog counts as one source, and no cloud is read through two for the same GPU. Euro prices are converted at the European Central Bank's rate of the day.
  2. Filter. Where a source shows capacity, a provider counts for a GPU only if one of its offers had capacity at some collection that day; its posted prices then all count, so an offer selling out does not read as a price change. Asks more than 2× from their marketplace's median and prices more than 2.5× from the GPU's historical reference are left out. A marketplace counts for a GPU only with at least 3 usable asks from at least 2 hosts.
  3. Check. A provider's price that moves more than 35% from its 14-day median is held out until the new level has lasted 3 days, unless the market moved with it: net of the median move of at least 3 other sources, it moved less than 35%. A move shared by most of the clouds read through one catalog, and not by other sources, is treated as that catalog's error and stays held.
  4. Standardize. Each price is divided by factors for how it differs from the benchmark: form factor and memory, GPUs per rental, region and CPU. Factors are estimated weekly over 28 days from providers that price both configurations on the same day, and need comparisons from at least 2 providers, or 5 matched groups for region and CPU. Without them, a price with another form factor or memory is left out and other differences are not adjusted.
  5. Average. Each provider's prices are averaged, so a provider counts once however many listings it has. A provider with no price on a day is carried for up to 7 days, moved by the other providers' average change.
  6. Chain. The index moves by the geometric mean of the price changes of providers priced both on the day and on the last published day:index today = index last × geometric mean of (provider average today ÷ provider average last)Itoday=Ilast×(∏i=1npˉi,todaypˉi,last)1/nI_{\text{today}} = I_{\text{last}} \times \left( \prod_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\bar{p}_{i,\text{today}}}{\bar{p}_{i,\text{last}}} \right)^{1/n}Itoday​=Ilast​×(i=1∏n​pˉ​i,last​pˉ​i,today​​)1/nwhere pˉi\bar{p}_ipˉ​i​ is the average price of provider iii and nnn is the number of providers priced on both days. Both averages use today's standardization factors, so a recalibration does not move the index, and providers joining or leaving do not move it either.
FactorCurrent values

Publication. A value needs at least 5 matched providers, 3 of them priced that day, so no provider weighs more than 20%. A new provider counts after 14 days of collection; the 15 added by version 4.1 count at once, from their second day of prices. If no value was published in the previous 7 days, the index restarts at the cross-section average: the mean of all provider averages with the most extreme ones clipped.

Also published each day: the cross-section average and the quartiles of the provider averages, and monthly averages of the index in /data/index.json.

History. Live values start on 2026-10-23. Before that, H100 and A100 have daily history from 2025-11-07, rebuilt with this methodology from the posted prices in SkyPilot's open price catalog, 5 to 8 providers a day; only these two have 90 days of it without a break. Earlier, and for H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000, history is weekly: GetDeploying's on-demand median across providers, in weeks with at least 5. Each earlier series is scaled to meet the later one, so a change of source does not move the index.

Token Price Index

One index for each of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Meta, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, DeepSeek, Z.ai and Xiaomi, the top 10 companies in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index in October 2026, with DeepSeek always included. A day's value is the average price of the company's paid models, weighted by their tokens that day:index = Σ (tokens × price) ÷ Σ tokensI=∑jqj Pj∑jqjI = \frac{\sum_{j} q_j \, P_j}{\sum_{j} q_j}I=∑j​qj​∑j​qj​Pj​​where qjq_jqj​ is the number of tokens of model jjj that day and PjP_jPj​ is its blended price.

  • Tokens are each model's daily prompt and completion tokens in OpenRouter's daily rankings of the top 50 models, used only to weight a company's models against each other.
  • Prices are the company's own posted prices at base rates, without cache, batch, priority or long-context pricing. Since 2026-10-22 they are read from the company's own endpoint on OpenRouter shortly after each UTC day ends. A model's input and output prices per 1M tokens are blended 3 to 1:blended price = (3 × input price + output price) ÷ 4P=3 Pin+Pout4P = \frac{3\,P_{\text{in}} + P_{\text{out}}}{4}P=43Pin​+Pout​​
  • Models that count are paid text models. Free variants, batch tiers, embedding and image models, and OpenAI's and Google's open-weight releases, gpt-oss and Gemma, are left out. A model with published weights counts only while the company itself serves it, since other hosts sell it too.
  • Coverage. A value is published only when models with a known price carry at least 80% of the tokens that count.

Real bills are usually lower than this list-price blend, because cached input costs a fraction of the base rate. The 3:1 blend is fixed because public data does not show each model's mix.

History. Daily from 2025-01-01, at each day's price from the dated history at llm-prices.com by Simon Willison, or a retired preview's announced price; a model with neither is priced at today's price, assuming it never changed. Where a company's own records date when it served each version, as DeepSeek's change log, Xiaomi's update log, Moonshot AI's model list and an Alibaba notice do, those dates decide which versions count, at the prices the company announced or else llm-prices.com's. A version served free does not count. Otherwise an open-weight model the company serves today counts from its release, and a day is left empty when versions of unknown service or price carry more than 20% of the tokens. DeepSeek's history uses its off-peak base rates and starts on 2026-08-17, the first full day of its current pricing. Where history meets the live index, on 2026-10-22, both give identical values.

Listing

A GPU or company is listed once it has a price and a month of history, so every row has its 1W and 1M change. DeepSeek is always listed. MI300X is collected but not yet published, because fewer than 5 providers price it.

Trending

The Trending tab lists the GPUs by the strength of their price trend over the last 13 weeks, strongest first, whether the price is rising or falling.

  1. Prices. The GPU's index on 13 dates a week apart, ending with the latest value (during the day, the provisional value).
  2. Line. A straight line fitted by least squares to the logarithms of those prices, week by week:ln(price) = intercept + slope × weekln⁡pk=a+b k+ek,k=0,1,…,12\ln p_k = a + b\,k + e_k, \qquad k = 0, 1, \ldots, 12lnpk​=a+bk+ek​,k=0,1,…,12where pkp_kpk​ is the price in week kkk, bbb is the fitted slope and eke_kek​ are the residuals. The slope is the trend's speed, shown per month:speed per month = e^(slope × 52 ÷ 12) − 1speed=e52 b/12−1\text{speed} = e^{52\,b/12} - 1speed=e52b/12−1
  3. Score. The slope divided by its standard error, the t-statistic of the slope: large when the price moved steadily one way, small when it moved little or back and forth.score = slope ÷ standard error of the slopet=bSE⁡(b)t = \frac{b}{\operatorname{SE}(b)}t=SE(b)b​SE⁡(b)=∑kek2 / (13−2)∑k(k−6)2\operatorname{SE}(b) = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_k e_k^2 \,/\, (13 - 2)}{\sum_k (k - 6)^2}}SE(b)=∑k​(k−6)2∑k​ek2​/(13−2)​​

Strength. Strong: a score of 4 or more, up or down. Moderate: 2 to 4. Weak: under 2, a move noise alone often makes. The arrow shows the direction. A GPU with less than 12 weeks of history has no score and is listed last.

Why this measure. On the index history, from 24 January to 26 September 2026, the GPU with the strongest score kept its direction over the next 4 weeks in 29 of 36 weeks, and following it gained 2.3% on average. The GPU with the largest 1-week change kept its direction in 11 of 26 weeks, and following it lost 1.1%: large weekly moves in GPU rental prices tend to partly reverse, while steady 13-week trends more often continued. One year of six GPUs is a small sample, so this is evidence, not a forecast. Trending is information, not investment advice.

Break-even throughput and gross margin

Each model's page shows its break-even throughput on each GPU: the tokens per second one GPU must generate, sold at the model's posted prices, for its revenue to cover the GPU's rental price today. Each GPU's page shows the same for every model in the Token Price Index. The gross margin calculator on each model's page compares the revenue one GPU earns in an hour with its rental price.

  1. Revenue per GPU-hour. The tokens one GPU generates in an hour, sold at the model's blended price:revenue per GPU-hour = throughput × 3,600 × blended price ÷ 1,000,000R=3600×T×P106R = \frac{3600 \times T \times P}{10^{6}}R=1063600×T×P​ The calculator also works the other way, from a revenue to the throughput that earns it:throughput = revenue per GPU-hour × 1,000,000 ÷ (3,600 × blended price)T=106×R3600×PT = \frac{10^{6} \times R}{3600 \times P}T=3600×P106×R​
  2. Gross profit per GPU-hour. Revenue less the GPU's rental price:gross profit per GPU-hour = revenue per GPU-hour − GPU rental priceG=R−CG = R - CG=R−C
  3. Gross margin. Gross profit as a share of revenue:gross margin = gross profit ÷ revenue per GPU-hourM=GR=1−CRM = \frac{G}{R} = 1 - \frac{C}{R}M=RG​=1−RC​
  4. Break-even throughput. The throughput at which revenue equals the rental price, so gross profit is zero:break-even throughput = GPU rental price × 1,000,000 ÷ (3,600 × blended price)TBE=106×C3600×PT_{\text{BE}} = \frac{10^{6} \times C}{3600 \times P}TBE​=3600×P106×C​

where TTT is throughput in tokens per second per GPU, PPP is the model's blended price in USD per 1M tokens, CCC is the GPU's rental price in USD per GPU-hour (its GPU Price Index today), RRR and GGG are revenue and gross profit in USD per GPU-hour, and MMM is gross margin.

Example. At a rental price of $3.00 per GPU-hour and a blended price of $1.00 per 1M tokens, break-even throughput is 833 tokens per second per GPU. At 5,000 tokens per second, revenue is $18.00 per GPU-hour, gross profit $15.00 and gross margin 83%.

Throughput is entered by the visitor, or worked out from the revenue entered; Compute Screener does not measure it. It counts input and output tokens together, in the 3 to 1 mix of the blended price, and depends on the model, the GPU, the serving software, batch size and context length. For a deployment on many GPUs, it is the deployment's tokens per second divided by its number of GPUs. Worked out from a revenue, it is the throughput that earns that revenue at the 3 to 1 mix of posted prices; the mix, cache hits and discounts behind a company's reported revenue can differ, and so can its actual throughput.

Limits. Prices are the posted base rates of the Token Price Index, without cache or batch discounts. Gross margin here counts only the GPU's rental price as cost, not networking, storage, staff or idle time, and assumes the GPU generates that throughput for the whole hour.

Reported figures. A company's own figure is shown as the company reported it, without verification. DeepSeek reported overall revenue of US$38 per GPU-hour for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at its off-peak ("valley") prices, from a cluster serving 155 trillion tokens a day, in the deployment Q&A it published with its DeepInfer inference framework in October 2026. It does not say which GPUs earn it.

Data

Every value can be recomputed from these public files, kept for five years:

FileHolds
/data/records/<day>.json.gzEvery GPU price collected, at every collection
/data/trace/<day>.json.gzEach price used, with its factor, or left out, with the reason; provider averages, chain ratio and matched providers
/data/model.json, /data/stats.jsonStandardization factors and the comparisons behind them; validation references and imputation inputs
/data/index.json, /data/series.jsonLatest GPU values with their providers; full history
/data/token_trace/<day>.json.gz, /data/tokens.json, /data/token_series.jsonEach company's models, tokens, prices and shares by day; latest values; full history
/data/legacy/History inputs and joins: skypilot_daily.json, getdeploying_weekly.json, history_link.json, token_history.json, llm_prices.json; every correction with its reason: restatements.json

Governance

Inputs. The GPU index uses posted prices and marketplace asks, which anyone can rent at, not executed transactions, which are not public. Indices of executed rentals can differ, usually lower, because large buyers negotiate their rates. Providers weigh equally because their rental volumes are not public.

Control. Values are calculated automatically, never set by judgment, and each run passes automated checks before it is published. A GPU index move above 5% in a day is reviewed, and a review can only confirm a value or correct an error.

Independence. No provider or company pays to be included. A Rent link that can earn a referral fee is marked "Paid link" and never affects the index or the order of providers. Compute Screener and the person who runs it hold no futures, swaps, prediction-market contracts or other instruments that settle on GPU rental or AI token prices, and no direct holdings in the providers or companies on this site.

Changes. A material change to the formula, inputs, filters, benchmark contracts or which providers and models count is announced here at least 14 days before it applies, with its version and date. Comments can be sent to the contact on the Privacy page, and a summary is published with the change. Corrections apply at once and are announced when made. Final values change only to correct an error or when a change of method restates history; each such change is recorded with its date, range and reason in /data/legacy/restatements.json. Latest: on 2026-10-24, version 4.1 added 15 providers, the capacity rule, the marketplace minimum and the market check on large moves, and compares each provider's prices on one set of factors. The owner applied it at once, without the usual 14 days' notice, and its new providers count at once instead of after 14 days of collection. H100 and A100 history was rebuilt with it. Earlier that day, version 4.0 introduced the chained GPU index and daily H100 and A100 history, and the token histories of DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Xiaomi and Alibaba were corrected from those companies' own records.

Third parties. The calculation runs on GitHub Actions and the site on Cloudflare Pages. If the ECB rate cannot be read, the last rate up to 7 days old is used, and after that euro prices are left out. A source that fails contributes nothing that run; the latest status of each is below.

Licence. The values and data on this site are licensed CC BY 4.0: anyone may reuse them, including commercially, with credit to "Compute Screener (computescreener.com)" (see the terms). Third-party data keeps its own terms: CC BY 4.0 for GetDeploying and OpenRouter, Apache-2.0 for SkyPilot's catalog.

Continuity. An index that cannot be calculated reliably is not published until it can be; its history stays available.

Questions and complaints go to the contact on the Privacy page.
